name: Tiger Data (Timescale, Inc. d/b/a Tiger Data)
origin_detail: Started in 2015 by Ajay Kulkarni (CEO) and Mike Freedman (CTO) building an IoT platform; they built TimescaleDB as a PostgreSQL extension for their own IoT data needs and launched it about 2017. Renamed TigerData/Tiger Data on 2025-06-17; legal name Timescale, Inc., d/b/a Tiger Data. HQ not confirmed in fetched pages.
openness_notes: TimescaleDB core is Apache-2.0; additional 'community' features are under the source-available Timescale License, which restricts offering them as a hosted service: open core (2). The launch-era licence (Apache-2.0 only) and the date the Timescale License was introduced were not confirmed in fetched pages.

license_history.note: Launch about 2017 ('five years ago' in a Feb 2022 company post); launch licence not confirmed directly.

license_history.license: Apache-2.0 core + source-available Timescale License for community features
license_history.note: Licence page dated 2020-09-24 cited by Wikipedia.

relicensing_events.outcome_note: Partial: the core stayed Apache-2.0. Year not confirmed in fetched pages. No fork found.

robustness: Built on PostgreSQL, a community-governed database, which lowers lock-in; the Apache-2.0 core is forkable. VC-backed single vendor; the company reports 2,000+ customer companies and 3 million databases (current about page).
openness_effect_assessment: Building on PostgreSQL, keeping an Apache-2.0 core and restricting only selected features let Timescale reach 500+ paying customers, 20x revenue growth over two years and a valuation over $1B by February 2022 (company figures), with no fork or licence backlash found.
key_takeaway: Tiger Data shows the 'extension' strategy: build on a community-governed open project (PostgreSQL), keep the core OSI-licensed, and restrict only cloud resale of add-ons. It avoided the fork dynamics of Elastic and Redis and reached unicorn status in 2022, then rebranded as Tiger Data in June 2025; no newer valuation was confirmed.
